observations: On the board crates are steering targets: ramming breaks them, so placement alone sets the difficulty (2-1-2 stagger, single-file pairs, offset pairs, 2x2 stagger).
Every board crate is paired with a hazard decision; rhythm is collect -> dodge -> collect.
Boost gates (whirlpool pairs) are kept free of crates; crates sit just before or after them.
One vertical test per board leg at most: the boosted-ramp box.
Checkpoints sit at docks; on-foot legs carry the checkpoints, board legs carry 15 of 23 main boxes.
Main course is light (23 of 74) because of the time-trial gem; 69% of boxes are in the bonus and gem course.
Box lines on the water trace the safe lane between mines and double as a racing line.
The only main-course life on the water sits inside the minefield.
The gem course recombines earlier lessons: single-use stepping boxes (now over water), Nitro rows around a checkpoint, outline/switch with a vehicle backtrack, floating Nitros, green ! at the exit.
Explosives are kept out of the main course: TNT only in the bonus, Nitros only in the gem course.

geometryObservations: Two locomotion modes alternate with docks as hinges, and every dock carries a checkpoint (C1 at the first board, C2 and C3 at the next two docks); no checkpoint sits on timed footing or on the board.

On foot the geometry is stepping stones over lethal water: ≈2.5–3 u slabs with 1–3.5 u gaps. Jump length alone is never the test; the coupling is — a sinking pillar (G-F1-a), a piranha in the gap (G-F1-b), a hippo that sinks on landing (G-F2-b), a flytrap's reach (P-F1-d).
Each coupling debuts once in a mild form and is then doubled: pillar ×1 → ×2; one flytrap at C1 → two in a row; one hippo → two offset; a piranha in F1 → again in F2.

Timed footing can be bypassed by skill: D2 dash-jumps the pillar gap without waiting, and F2's time-trial advice is not to wait for footholds — every timed crossing has a slow safe line and a fast line.

Board legs are slaloms on a ≈6–8 u channel: static mine lines are lane dividers (O-W1-a), whirlpool pairs are boost gates (O-W1-b), moving mines are timing gates (O-W2-c), and ramps add the vertical axis (P-W2-a, P-W2-b).
The board has a stop verb (turn sideways, POINT11), which is what makes moving-mine timing gates fair on a forced-motion vehicle.
Ramp 1 rewards maximum boost (the ? above its arc) and ramp 2 punishes it (mines beyond the log wall): the same object with opposite speed demands, 2–3 s apart.
Event cadence from D2's timer: on the board one decision every ≈2–3 s (whirlpools 0:23, mine line 0:21, ramp 1 0:18, field 0:16); on foot through the hippos one beat every ≈1.5–2 s (0:35 → 0:30).
The enemies behave as platforms and timers rather than fighters: flytraps are planted, piranhas leap on a cycle inside gaps, hippos are footing with a fuse. Nothing chases.

The gem course escalates both grammars: on foot a moving island, a hippo, a consumable crate bridge over lethal water and a checkpoint between two Nitro rows; on the board Nitros floating where crates usually are and an upstream switch that forces an about-face.
The bonus teaches a move the main course never needs (sliding under a steel ceiling, P-B-b): side skills live in side rooms.
Water is the only killer on foot and the banks wall the board legs, so every hazard is in the channel itself; there are no side drops to manage.
geometryTransfer: Causeway over `lethal` water: 3 m square `platform` tiles with 1.2–3.5 m gaps (1–3 crates); bridge one 3.5 m gap with a 1.7 m `phasepad` (cycle 3–4 s, on-share 0.5) — the 5.6 m running jump also clears the whole gap, which keeps a fast line for time trials.

Hippo steps: `crumble` pads (shake 0.3–0.5 s, ≈2.3 m wide) standing in the water, first one alone, then two offset 2.5 m sideways and 3 m apart for the zig-zag double; they return after 10 s, so a failed attempt can be retried without a checkpoint.
Gap occupant without a new system: a `firetiki` beside a 2.5 m water gap whose sweep crosses the gap every 2–3 s plays the piranha — the jump is timed to its cycle while the tiles stay static.

Board slalom on a 7–9 m lane: a single-file row of 6 Nitro crates down the left third as the lane divider (never on the racing line), a boost gate of two `pit`s with a 2.5–3 m gap and a `speedpad` in the gap, and a `stone` patrolling across the lane (axis x) 6–8 m past a kicker's landing as the moving mine; the brake is the stop verb that makes it fair.

Ramp pair with opposite demands: kicker 1 with a crate floating above its landing arc that only a near-charged approach (≈23 m/s) reaches; kicker 2 in front of a 1.5–2 m wall with Nitro 10–12 m past it, so a charged launch overshoots into it and a cruise launch (12 m/s, ≈6.6 m of air) lands short.
Put a checkpoint on every dock-like transition between foot and board, never on timed footing; keep the board leg itself free of saves (≈20 s per leg, as in W2).
